issues.legal_issue: A preliminary decree in a partition suit cannot be declared void for fraud absent appropriate pleadings and evidence establishing fraud.
Findings on title in a partition suit are not binding on third parties who assert independent claims to the property.

In proceedings under Order XXI Rules 97–101 of the Code of Civil Procedure, an executing court cannot determine title claims by third parties asserting independent title; it may assess whether their claim is bona fide and independent.
A preliminary decree in a partition suit declares undivided shares and does not itself allot specific parcels of property or confer title to them.
The properties at issue were not established to be inheritable Mathruka property, and the findings in the preliminary decree did not establish otherwise.
The claim petitioners established a bona fide independent claim to the land based on the evidence of pattas and related possession records.
The findings concerning the claim petitioners’ title to the land do not bind the State, whose claim to the remaining land was not determined in these proceedings.
